{{nihongo|'''Kiyama Shrine'''|城山神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sanuki Province]].

'''Shiroyama Shrine'' (Kiyama Shrine) is located in Fuchu Town, {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture|Q161454|qid=Q161454}}{{ill|Sakaide, Kagawa|Q855059|qid=Q855059}}. {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}) and {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old shrine rank}} is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}}.

=== Enshrined God ===
The following three deities are enshrined.
; Main enshrined deity
:* {{ill|Kamukushi no Mikoto|Q11590432|qid=Q11590432|lt=Kamikushi no Mikoto}}
:: In some literature, he is also written as ``Kamikushi no Miko.'' === History ===
[[File:Myojin-bara Ruins in Kiyama.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Myojinbara Ruins}}]]

=== Founding ===
According to the shrine's legend, the enshrined deity {{ill|Kamukushi no Mikoto|Q11590432|qid=Q11590432|lt=Kamikushibetsu no Mikoto}} was appointed {{ill|sanukinokuninomiyatsuko|Q21653200|qid=Q21653200}} during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ar|الإمبراطور كيكو|arz|الامبراطور كيكو|azb|کیکو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Keikō|cs|Keikó|de|Keikō|es|Keikō Tennō|fa|امپراتور کیکو|fr|Keikō (empereur)|hr|Keikō|hu|Keikó japán császár|id|Kaisar Keikō|it|Keikō|ja|景行天皇|ka|კეიკო|ko|게이코 천황|nds|Keikō|nl|Keiko (keizer)|no|Keiko (keiser)|pl|Keikō|pt|Imperador Keikō|ru|Император Кэйко|sh|Car Keikō|simple|Emperor Keikō|sl|Cesar Kejko|sv|Keiko (kejsare)|th|จักรพรรดิเคโก|tl|Emperador Keikō|tr|Keikō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кейко|uz|Imperator Keikō|vi|Thiên hoàng Keikō|yo|Emperor Keikō|zh|景行天皇|zh_min_nan|Keikô Thian-hông|zh_yue|景行天皇|qid=Q329723}} for his work in exterminating evil fish in the southern seas. He later built a mansion in Shiroyama and lived there, but died at the age of 120 in {{ill|Emperor Chūai|Q179971|qid=Q179971}}. Later, a shrine was built to enshrine the divine spirit, and this is the beginning of our company. <ref name=kosho> ``Sanuki Kokukansha Kosho'' (from the Shiroyama Shrine section of ``Place Names of Kagawa Prefecture''). </ref><ref name=yuisho>Shrine history book. </ref>.Regarding {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamikushibetsu no Mikoto}}, "{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}}" also says, "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamikushio no Mikoto}} (same as Kamikushibetsu no Mikoto) <ref>In the Nihon Shoki, in the 4th year of Emperor Keiko's reign, it is written, ``Next wife Isokawahime, Prince Ikami Kushi, Prince Inase Irihiko.Her older brother Prince Kamikushi, also the founder of the creation of Sanuki Province.'' </ref>. In addition, in "{{ill|Kujiki|Q2716751|qid=Q2716751}}" and "{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|Q133833194|qid=Q133833194}}," "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Suri Hore no Mikoto}}, the grandson of Kamikushibetsu no Mikoto III, was the son of Sanuki Kunizo in the {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997}} period. <ref>Kokuzōhonki ({{ill|Kujiki|Q2716751|qid=Q2716751}}, Vol. 10) Sanuki Kunizojo ``{{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Karushima Toyomincho}} reign.Emperor Keiko, Kamikushio III, Grandson, Noriyoshi no Mikoto, and Kunizo.'' </ref>, {{ill|sanukinokuninomiyatsuko|Q21653200|qid=Q21653200}} are the same in that they are the ancestors of the clan.

Also, according to the shrine's legend, it was originally enshrined at the Myojinbara Ruins ({{ill|Kiyama Shrine|Q11426120|qid=Q11426120|lt=described later}}) which remains on one peak of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiroyama}}. Since there are still several megaliths in Myojinhara, it is assumed that rituals have been held there since ancient times. </ref>.

=== Outline ===
In {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi}}, "{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}" {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} 1st Year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}) Article (Japan)|Q1075635|Jōkan}} In the 7th year ({{ill|865|Q30350|qid=Q30350}}) article, there is an article about the promotion of {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} to "Shiroyama Kami".

{{ill|Enchō|de|Enchō|fa|انچو|fr|Ère Enchō|ia|Encho|id|Enchō|ja|延長 (元号)|ko|엔초|ru|Энтё|simple|Enchō|sr|Енчо|tr|Enchō|uk|Ентьо|zh|延長 (日本)|zh_yue|延長 (年號)|qid=Q1327274|lt=extended}} "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}) {{jali nk|Engishiki Shinmeicho|Q11064932|Shinmeicho}}, {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682}}{{ill|Aya district|Q11658001|qid=Q11658001}} "Shiroyama Shrine" It is listed as ``Meishin Taisha'' and is listed as {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}. In addition to our company, there are only three {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}} in {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682}}: {{ill|Tamura Shrine|Q11576976|qid=Q11576976}} and {{ill|Awai Shrine|Q11604560|qid=Q11604560}}. The reason why it was revered in this way seems to have been related to the fact that {{ill|Sanuki Kokubun-ji|Q1101226|qid=Q1101226|lt=Sanuki Kokufu}} was located at the foot of Mt. Shiroyama <ref name=chimei/>, and there is also a theory that it served as the protector of the prefecture and the provincial governor <ref name=chimei/>.According to "Sugaya Bunso", in {{ill|Ninna|Q1346317|qid=Q1346317}}4 ({{ill|AD 888|Q29956|qid=Q29956}}), {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}} of {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province}} built a castle. Praying for rain at the Yama Shrine <ref> "{{ill|Kanke Bunsō|Q109359816|qid=Q109359816}}" Shiroyama Shinbun Festival held on May 6, 1947 ([http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/550401.html Shiroyama Shrine] (see Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection). </ref>. It is said that the prayer was successful and brought about a bountiful harvest.

The state of the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} is unknown, but it appears to have gradually declined, and then in the first year of {{ill|Jōji|Q1146153|qid=Q1146153}} ({{jalink|13 It was destroyed by fire during the battle between {{ill|Hosokawa Yoriyuki|Q1139739|qid=Q1139739}} and {{ill|Hosokawa Kiyouji|Q11605934|qid=Q11605934|lt=Kiyoshi}} in 1962|Q6166}}.<ref name=chimei/>. Therefore, only the divine object was moved to the land of Inna ({{Coord|34|17|43.51|N|133|55|03.35|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Inna (temporary transfer location)}}), a small shrine was built, and it was later moved to the current location <ref name=kosho/>.

After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, it was ranked as {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}} in {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine rank system}}.

=== God level ===
* {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} November 7th, 1st year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), from upper 6th rank to lower rank of junior 5th rank (``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}'') - Written as ``Shiroyama no Kami.''
*October 9, 7th year of Jogan ({{ill|865|Q30350|qid=Q30350}}), the first rank of Jugoi (``Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'') - Written as ``Shiroyama no Kami.''

== Setsusha ==
'''Precincts end shrine'''
[[File:Shiroyama Shrine (Sakaide City) Precincts Amake Tenmangu.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Amake Tenmangu}}]]
* Amaketenmangu Shrine
*: The enshrined deity is {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}}. {{ill|Ninna|Q1346317|qid=Q1346317}} It began with Michizane's {{ill|Rainmaking (ritual)|Q477738|qid=Q477738}}, which was worshiped in gratitude.

=== Related locations ===
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiroyama}} (Kiyama)
*: A mountain with an altitude of 462m located between {{ill|Sakaide, Kagawa|Q855059|qid=Q855059}} and {{ill|Marugame, Kagawa|Q460835|qid=Q460835}}, rising behind Shiroyama Shrine. It is said that {{ill|ancient mountain fortress in Japan|Q6431764|qid=Q6431764}} ({{ill|Kiyama Castle|Q46999719|qid=Q46999719|lt=Sanuki Shiroyama Castle}}) was built on top of the mountain, and the mountain name ``Shiroyama'' is derived from this. The remains of castles can be seen throughout the area, and are designated as national historic sites. </ref>. In addition, {{ill|Lithic reduction|Q1142470|qid=Q1142470|lt=stone tools}} were also excavated near the summit of the mountain. </ref>It is known that people have lived there since ancient times. It was also used as a place for rituals, as shown in the Myojingahara ruins below.
* Myojinbaru Ruins
** Location: Southeast peak of Shiroyama ({{Coord|34|17|33.65|N|133|53|57.83|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Myojinbaru ruins (former enshrinement site)}})*: It is said to be the former enshrinement site of Shiroyama Shrine. Because it is dotted with huge stones, it is thought to have been a sacred place since ancient times as a place where gods descended, and it is speculated that rituals have been held here since ancient times. It is also said that {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}} prayed for rain here.
* {{ill|Kamukushi no Mikoto|Q11590432|qid=Q11590432|lt=King Kamikushi Tomb}}
** Location: {{ill|Takamatsu|Q200707|qid=Q200707}}Mure Town, Mure ({{Coord|34|20|35.28|N|134|07|17.22|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Kamikushio Official Tomb}})
*: {{ill|Kamukushi no Mikoto|Q11590432|qid=Q11590432|lt=Prince Kamikushi}}, which is under the jurisdiction of the Imperial Household Agency.
* {{ill|Tsuzumigaoka Shrine|Q11678981|qid=Q11678981}}
** Location: Fuchu-cho, Sakaide City ({{Coord|34|17|35.80|N|133|54|59.45|E|region:JP-37_type:landmark|name=Tsumioka Shrine (Kamikushio Tomb?)}})
*: According to the Shiroyama Shrine biography, the site of Tsuzumioka Shrine is {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|Q11268718|qid=Q11268718}}, and is also said to be the tomb of {{ill|Kamukushi no Mikoto|Q11590432|qid=Q11590432|lt=Kamikushibetsu no Mikoto}}<ref name=yuisho/><ref>In the Tsuzumioka section of ``Place Names of Kagawa Prefecture'', it is written as {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|simple|Round Kofun|zh|圓墳|qid=Q11394747}} (the relationship with Kamikushibetsu no Mikoto is not pointed out). </ref>.
